tags.name: Lighthouse
tags.qa_note: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-17: Previous data (wall dive, 30m, thresher sharks, hawksbill turtles on wall face) contradicted by 3+ independent sources (diveplanit.com, malapascua-diving.com, malapascuaisland.com, kokaysmalditodiveresort.com), which consistently describe Lighthouse as a shallow (~6-12m) reef/coral garden famous for a dusk mandarin fish mating dive, not a 30m wall. Corrected site_type, depth, difficulty and rewrote description. This appears to have been conflated with the nearby wreck or another wall site.

tags.name: North Point
tags.qa_note: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-17: Sources conflict on North Point's character. kokaysmalditodiveresort.com and malapascua-diving.com describe an 8-24m reef suited to Open Water divers with macro life (frogfish, crabs, nudibranchs). dive-the-world.com describes a deeper (15-30m) current-swept wall/slope for experienced divers with pelagics (barracuda, tuna, Napoleon wrasse, reef sharks). Both are cited in the markdown rather than picking one. Previous data (35m Advanced pinnacle with hammerhead sharks/dogtooth tuna) was not corroborated by any source and was removed.

tags.name: Monad Shoal
tags.qa_note: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-17: Wikipedia and dive-operator sources describe the shoal's flat top at 20-24m with cleaning-station activity concentrated around 32m, rising from a ~200m drop-off and terminating ~15m below the surface. Previous depth field (50m) did not match any source's typical dive profile and contradicted the markdown's own Dive Profile section (which already said 'typically 30 meters'). tags.name: Japanese Ship Wreck
tags.qa_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-17: Coordinates (~150-200m from the 'Lighthouse' site, OSM already flagged 'location approximate') and site character match the wreck locally known as 'Lighthouse Wreck'. 3 independent sources (padi.com, malapascua-diving.com, dumagueteinfo.com) agree it is a WWII Japanese landing craft carrying a cement cargo, bombed before reaching shore, lying broken in two pieces in ~3-5m of water. A 4th source (kokaysmalditodiveresort.com) describes it more generally as a Japanese warship that was hiding and was bombed, giving a max depth of 7m, without the landing-craft/cement detail - this conflict is noted in the markdown rather than resolved by guessing. No source gives a vessel name, build date, length, or tonnage, so none is stated. Previous JSON depth (33m) and markdown content (batfish schools, cargo-hold lionfish, 18-33m profile) did not match any source and have been replaced.
